🥳 We are happy to announce the creation of the Adriatic-Baltic-Black-Azov seas Student Association! 

















🌍 ABBA is a collective youth initiative that aims to bring together students and youths from Eastern European states, exploring common cultural and historical heritage, as well as outlining the academic importance of political developments of these states at Leiden University @universiteitleiden

















🗣 Together, we will organize events to share and discuss our culture, history, and politics with the student community. 

















🙌 Join us to dive into the world of magical countries and nations located between the Adriatic, Baltic, Black, and Azov seas!

📌 Updated version is pinned 








❗️ Our main goals are: 

















1️⃣: Spread awareness of member countries' politics, culture, and history among LU students. 

















For years, Eastern Europe got little-to-no coverage in university curricula and student-led events. By starting this association, we aim to raise awareness of our countries’ present-day achievements, as well as historical and cultural richness, through events, discussions, and festivals. 

















2️⃣: Promote an academic focus on member states' political developments. 

















Some of our countries’ political developments have stricken the news, however, little is known to the general public besides the headlines. We strive to share the knowledge of the intricate workings of our politics through an academic lens here at LU. 

















3️⃣: Maintain attention on Russia's invasion of Ukraine. 

















For more than a year, Ukraine has been bravely defending its right to freedom and democracy. We aim to do everything possible to support Ukrainian students and to remind the LU community about the hardships that Ukrainian people face. 

















📣 Stay tuned for our upcoming events!

Today marks 1000 days since russia’s invasion of Ukraine – 1000 days of bravery in fighting for national and territorial integrity and the broader principle of independence. In this context, we encourage to also be aware of the connotations in academia that undermine the notions of sovereignty and independence. The attention has been brought to the regional maps of “Europe” and “russia and Eurasia” displayed at the Area Fair for International Studies students of Leiden University on November 1. Baltic States are placed within the map of “russia and Eurasia,” while unacceptably being entirely omitted from the map of Europe. Such depictions not only fail to reflect the geopolitical realities and internationally established territorial units but also risk perpetuating narratives that undermine the principles of independence and self-determination, principles that are central to academic integrity and responsible scholarship.

















An official letter has been sent to Leiden University, establishing a concern from NLT, ABBA, NLYA, and fellow youth. We invite to engage with this issue critically and to reflect on the major points of the statement above.

Decentralization unlocks local governance and builds local trust.

















Last week, and Ukrainian Institute had the great honour and joy of hosting a discussion on Community Resilience During Wartime with Tymofii Brik, a Ukrainian sociologist and the current Rector of the Kyiv School of Economics, at Leiden University - Institute of Public Administration.

















🔍 Brik’s recent research explores 𝐡𝐨𝐰 𝐔𝐤𝐫𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐢𝐚𝐧 𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐦𝐮𝐧𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐞𝐬 𝐡𝐚𝐯𝐞 𝐝𝐞𝐦𝐨𝐧𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐫𝐞𝐦𝐚𝐫𝐤𝐚𝐛𝐥𝐞 𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐫𝐨𝐮𝐠𝐡𝐨𝐮𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐰𝐚𝐫, 𝐰𝐢𝐭𝐡 𝐚 𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐢𝐜𝐮𝐥𝐚𝐫 𝐟𝐨𝐜𝐮𝐬 𝐨𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐞𝐟𝐟𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐬 𝐨𝐟 𝐝𝐞𝐜𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐫𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐳𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐫𝐞𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐦𝐬.

















One of the key outcomes of Ukraine’s 2015–2019 decentralization reform - which significantly expanded local autonomy and strong civic participation in budgeting - was a measurable increase in social capital. 

















This transformation was critical in Ukraine’s wartime resilience. These decentralization reforms empowered local governance, fostered trust, and enabled communities not just to endure but to act with agency, strength, and effectiveness.
